notes.title: Wingman AI Beta Update
notes.content:
This update adds the following...

1. Wingmen will now consider all available weapons when deciding which one to use including any turreted guns when the range to target is 2,000m or less. 

2. Updated the formula for calculating the best weapon to use so that the closer the target is the more likely the A.I. will choose to use turreted guns. This is balanced by also taking into account the available number of missiles so the A.I. may still opt for missiles if it has lots of them available.

3. A.I. will now report back "No Suitable Weapon" if the target is outside all available weapon ranges.

4. New Command "Flight RTB" (F4 by default) will instruct your wingman to return to base and land.

5. Updated some of the Targeting Pod code to try and fix the bug where targeting pods get stuck in the top right corner and cannot be moved unless you use the "Reset Targeting Pod" command. This seems to only effect TrackIR users.

----

The next thing I want to do is improve the "Attack My Target" command so that the A.I. will close to attack range if the target isn't too far away as well as smoothing out the transition to hover if the order is given when the wingman is moving at speed.

I also want to add in a "Search & Destroy" command which will instruct the A.I. to engage targets within a certain area.

These final 2 command should make the A.I. fairly competent and I will then be looking at some U.I. changes to integrate the commands to allow GamePad/Hotas users to issue commands more easily. This system will also allow you to setup voice commands via something like VoiceAttack.

Finally, I will be adding in the calculations for D.P. usage and applying the XP earned to the correct pilots etc.

Once this is done I think the current beta can be moved into the live branch. ːsteamsunnyː

notes.title: Wingman AI Beta Update
notes.content:
Quick update for the Wingman Beta...

1. Pilot and Copilots are now selectable for your wingman. This actually doesn't do anything in reality and you can also select the same pilots/copilots as your main helicopter at the moment.

2. Fixed a bug that could cause your wingman to get stuck in an "Attacking your target", "Target destroyed" radio call loop if you gave them an additional "Attack My Target" command while they were engaging a target.

If for some reason your wingman misses or the target requires multiple strikes to destroy it (e.g. APKWS vs T-62M) then your wingman will continue to fire until that target is destroyed. However, they will only fire one missile/rocket at a time currently.

3. Implemented a "Resume Mission" system so that if you give your wingman a "Move To", "Move To My Position" or "Form Up" command and THEN give them an "Attack my target" command they will resume their previous orders once the target is destroyed.

4. Smoothed out the "Attack my target" command if your wingman is moving. Instead of overshooting the attack position, then turning around etc before finally engaging the target they will now slow down in a sensible fashion before shooting. It is also possible that if they will fire while moving if the angles all match up for a good launch.

5. Fixed a bug where your wingman would not move to the correct position when issuing a "Move there" commanded. The position error would get worse the higher the wingman was flying so wasn't really visible on the Lush Desert terring but was significant on certain parts of Norway.

[u]Next Update[/u]

Tomorrow I'm going to look at re-designing the Mission Planning screen to give you a better overview of your selected helicopters, their weapons and assigned pilots. I think it is nearly time for a UI overhaul in general...

notes.title: Wingman AI Beta Update
notes.content:
This update adds the following....

1. Wingmen can now talk! They'll let you know what they are doing and respond to commands so that you know they are doing what they are supposed to be!

2. Pilot voices - there is now a drop down in the Sierra Hotel area to select which voice to use for your pilots. At the moment there is only the default male voice but I'll be adding more shortly.

3. Added "Move To Position" command (F8 by default). Simply point your targeting pod at a spot, lock on and then send this command and your wingman will move to that position. Final orientation and altitude is based on [u]YOUR[/u] orientation/altitude when you issued the command.

4. Added "Move To My Position" command (F9 by default). This will instruct your wingman to fly to your exact current position. Final orientation and altitude is based on [u]YOUR[/u] orientation/altitude when you issued the command. - just make sure you've moved before they arrive!

These extra commands should open up some extra tactical options and make your wingman a little more useful.

"Move To Position" should have fairly obvious uses allowing you to reposition your wingman where ever you want. You can get them to scout areas ahead or setup at a firing position ready for you to designate targets. If they get into trouble you can quickly recall them by using the "Flight Form Up" command. 

"Move To My Position" is designed to allow you to quickly get your wingman to move to safe positions as the stance they will take when they get there will be exactly the same as yours was when you issued the command. 

e.g. If you are ahead of your wingman spotting targets for them to engage you can instantly tell them to move to your current hiding spot while you move forward to find another vantage point.

Tomorrow I shall be integrating the pilot/co-pilot system for your wingman so that you'll be able to select who is flying. This will also mean that wingmen will start to gain experience from flying missions with you. 

[u]However, XP will be divided equally between all pilots/co-pilots that take part in the mission[/u].

This will reduce the amount of XP gained by each individual pilot per mission, although it will be balanced out a bit by having more firepower to destroy more stuff, but it also provides an good incentive to use fewer helicopters on a mission.

notes.title: WingmanAI Beta Update
notes.content:
This update adds the ability to take a single wingman on missions!  ːsteamhappyː ːsteamhappyː

It's fairly barebones at the moment but should provide a solid foundation to build a good A.I. system.

1. You can now select a wingman on the Mission Planning screen. You don't need to assign a pilot or gunner at the moment.

2. To arm your wingman you can click on the two buttons next to the Flight Name on the arming screen to switch between helicopters.

3. Wingmen are cleared to use turreted guns and guided munitions only! They cannot engage with gunpods or rocketpods at the moment.

4. Yout now have 3 main commands....

[list]
[*] "Flight Form Up" - F5 by default. Instructs your wingman to form up and fly in formation. Also instructs them to take off at the start of the mission.

[*] "Flight Hold Position" - F6 by default. Instructs your wingman to stay put. If you send this command while flying at speed they will gently coast to a stop.

[*] "Attack My Target" - F7 by default. Instructs your wingman to attack your target. This command is best used while stationary. Your wingman will orientate themselves towards the target and then engage using their selected weapon. Once the target has been destroyed they will resume their last order.
[/list]

5. Wingmen currently do not consume any DP points at all!

While you only seem to have very limited commands it is possible to use them quite creatively. e.g. Take the Kiowa yourself and loadup your wingman with Hellfires. You can then tell them to stay put and fly ahead scouting for and then designating targets for them to attack.

You can load multiple weapon types on your Wingman's aircraft. They will calculate the best weapon to use based on the target type and the available ammo & cost of the weapon. 

For example if your wingman has APKWS and Hellfires then they will tend to prefer using APKWS against lightly armoured targets saving the Hellfires for tanks. 

Wingmen are still pretty dumb when it comes to avoiding things which is why you can only have one at the moment! I'll be improving that as we move forward.

[u]Known Bugs[/u]

1. If you issue a 2nd "Attack My Target" command while your wingman is currently attacking another target then they won't resume their flight orders correctly afterwards and will perform a rapid decent into the ground. You can issue a Flight Form Up command again to get the back into the fight!

notes.title: Wingman A.I. Beta Update
notes.content:
This update enables the formation flying A.I. for testing purposes and is really just a show case of how the A.I. manages the fairly complex task of flying and staying in formation.

[u]Spawning Wingmen[/u]
There is now a button (F5 by default) to spawn in up to 3 A.I. wingmen. The wingmen will fly an unarmed version of whatever helicopter you are currently in.

It is best to spawn them in once you have gained at least 10-20m of altitude to prevent them colliding with objects around the base.

Their basic A.I. settings should allow your wingmen to fly in a V formation with you.

[u]A.I. Abilities[/u]

1. Formation station keeping at hover / very low speeds. The wingmen will maintain relative position and heading without breaking formation while at low speeds. This means you can rotate your helicopter slowly and they formation will rotate around with you correctly. 

You can even fly slowly backwards and they will maintain formation.

At low speeds the A.I. has no minimum altitude which makes it perfect of NOE (Nap of the Earth) flying.

2. At high speed the A.I. will dynamically spread out and also increase their altitude to a safer height if they are too low. It is currently set reasonably high to ensure they don't do anything silly like flying into the ground!

3. When transitioning from high speed to hover / low speed the A.I. should tighten formation smoothly. 

However, during very aggressive maneuvers it is possible for the A.I. to overshoot their formation position but they should work out what they need to do and re-join fairly smoothly without having to do a "fly around".

4. A.I. will defend themselves from missile attacks.

5. A.I. will not shoot at enemy units

6. A.I. can take damage from the enemy.

7. A.I. flies a slightly simplified physics model but are still constrained by the same weight, drag and engine power as you.

8. The A.I. can fly the Harrier in a hover but they will not transition into forward flight.

[u]Bugs[/u]

There's probably quite a few! Don't spawn the A.I. if you actually want to play and complete a mission successfully.

The main visible bug is the A.I.'s tendancy to oscillate forward/back and left/right while station keeping in the hover. I know what is causing that and should have that sorted A.S.A.P.

[u]Next Stage[/u]

Next stage is to integrate the wingmen into the mission planning area so you can select what aircraft the A.I. will fly and what weapons they will carry.

The plan is to have 3 flights available for any given mission...

Flight 1 (Rotor Wing)
Any 1 - 4 Helicopters from the available helicopter pool. This will be your main attack flight.

Flight 2 (Fixed Wing)
Any 1 - 2 Aircraft from the available aircraft pool. This will be your close air support flight

Flight 3 (Rotor Wing)
Any 1 - 2 Helicopters from the Utility Helicopter pool. This will be your troop / cargo / other transportation flight

This should give you great flexibility on you how deploy your forces for each mission.

notes.title: Detection System Integration into Main Branch
notes.content:
This is a big update for the default branch of the game and adds all the improvements and additions from the DetectionBeta branch.

[u]Quick Rundown of Improvements & Additions[/u]

1. New 9K330 Tor unit for REDFOR. This is a long range (12km) SACLOS Radar guided SAM missile.

2. New "HERO" external model for the Kiowa Warrior.

3. New Visual, Thermal, Radar (VTR) detection system where every unit in the game now has a unique 360 degree profile which determines its detectability via Visual, Thermal or Radar sources.

4. New AGM-144 Sidearm anti-radiation missile

5. Pulse and Doppler radar modelling which determines how well these Radar sources can detect you depending on your relative motion.

6. New flyable Harrier GR.9. This is essentially a test of the VTOL transition system which will be used on helicopters such as the Osprey. However, the Harrier also showcases how flyable fixed wing aircraft can be integrated into the game.

7. New Threat Display which now shows incoming and outgoing missiles as well as where Radar threats are originating from, their type and whether they have locked on to you.

8. New countermeasure system included working Chaff!

9. Various new options in the settings menu to tweak not only graphical settings but also how effective countermeasures are allowing you to tweak the gameplay to your preference.

10. Various optimisations to improve RAM/VRAM usage and improve frame rates overall.

[u]9K330 Tor[/u]

The 9K330 Tor is a long range (12km) SACLOS Radar guided missile which will definitely changes the way you approach missions. Flying high is now a risky manoeuvre when these SAM launchers are present in the mission area.

While they are long ranged and carry a big warhead you can employ lots of different tactics to defeat them.

[list]
[*] Stay low - Hiding behind terrain so that they never see you will always be the best option. 

[*] Use SACLOS against them - When the missile is launched the launching vehicle must maintain a constant lock on you to guide the missile in. Break that lock and the missile will not track you and you can do this by breaking line of sight (LOS), using Chaff or destroying the launching vehicle.

[*] Use the new AGM-144 Sidearm. It can strike Radar emissions up to 15km away!
[/list]

[u]Visual, Thermal, Radar (VTR) Detection System/u]

All units now have a unique 360 degree VTR profile. These profiles take into account physical sizes of the vehicle, how much heat they output and where this heat is visible from and also the Radar cross-section of the unit.

For example -  the AH-1Z helicopter has a much lower Visual detection value when viewed from the front or rear due to its narrow airframe. It also has a much lower Thermal profile when viewed from the front aspect than when viewed from the rear due to engine exhausts. Its Radar profile is, like most helicopters, pretty big from any angle due to the main rotor blades being a giant Radar reflector!

These systems make fairly minor differences between helicopters at the moment. However, when the Comanche makes and appearance then you will instantly see how much better its Thermal and Radar profile is.

[u]Pulse and Doppler Radar Simulation[/u]

Pulse and Doppler Radar systems are now simulated so that their ability to detect moving objects is now dependant on your relative movement direction.

Pulse Radar systems generate very weak returns when you are moving directly towards or away from them. However, they receive a very strong return if you are flying parallel to them.

Doppler Radars work the other way around easily detecting you when you move towards them but having more difficulty if you maintain a steady distance from them.

While this sounds great in theory, helicopters, in practice, have a major flaw in that the rotating blades of both the main rotor and tail rotor will ALWAYS be moving in the correct direction to send a strong return no matter the Radar type and, as such, you cannot "notch" a Radar in the same way that a fixed wing aircraft can.

The Harrier though [u]can[/u] "notch" a Tor quite effectively.

For reference...
The 9K330 Tor uses a Doppler Radar.
The Shilka uses a Pulse Radar.

[u]New Threat Display[/u]

The new Threat Display works in tandem with the new Radar types. Pulse Radars are identified with a double white circle pulse together with the standard yellow line whenever they are detected. Doppler Radars only have the yellow line.

The Threat Display is now also smart enough to mark detected Radar sources permanently allowing it to build up a picture of where most anti air defences are automatically.

[u]AGM-144 Sidearm[/u]

This new missile is designed to counter the Tor but it is also effective against the Shilka. It is a fire and forget weapon that will home in on the [u]1st Radar[/u] source that it detects. You simply fire the missile in the general direction and it will do the rest.

The Sidearm is capable of hitting the Tor up to 15km away depending on altitude and launch speed.

The Sidearm can be carried by all helicopters either on a single missile or dual missile rack. The Sidearm now replaces the Apache's and Viper's ability to mount Hellfires/TOW/APKWS on the wing tips which was never really realistic!

[u]Flyable Harrier GR.9[/u]

While this started out as a test of the VTOL transition system that will be required on other helicopters, it proved too much fun not to include in the game.

To take off you will need to climb to around 150m vertically in the same way as you would with a helicopter. Once at this altitude retract the landing gear and then point the nose down in a similar way to a helicopter to gain forward speed.

As you gain speed the VTOL system will automatically vector the thrust to the rear. At about 90kts you should be able to pull the nose up and start to gain altitude and speed. 

At around 150kts you will be in full aircraft mode and the Harrier can be flown like any other fixed wing aircraft.

[u]Next Beta[/u]

The next Beta will be focusing on the Wingman A.I. This A.I. will also power enemy helicopters so expect the mission areas to be come a lot more dynamic in the near future!

notes.title: DetectionSystem Beta Hotfix
notes.content: Fixes the turrets for both the AH-64A & AH-64B so they are correctly slaved to the targeting camera.

notes.title: Update for DetectionSystem Beta
notes.content:
This update adds the final few pieces to the VTR (Visual, Thermal Radar) detection system...

1. Radars Detectors / Radar Guided Missiles can now be "notched" depending on their radar type.
[list]
[*] Pulse Radar (Shilka): Generates weak returns when you're flying directly towards the Radar source but strong returns when flying perpendicular  to it.
[*] Doppler Radar (Tor): Generates weak returns when you're maintaining a fixed distance to it but strong returns when flying directly towards it.
[/list]

However, neither of these manoeuvres will have much effect for a helicopter because the spinning main rotor blades will always be moving in a direction that either Radar type can get a strong return from. 

The Harrier though can notch the Tor quite well and is a good example of how the whole Radar detection system will work in Stealth Fighter D.E.X.

2. I've swapped the Radar types of the Tor and Shilka around so the Tor now has a Doppler Radar and the Shilka now has a Pulse Radar. I believe this is now the correct way around.

3. Your threat display will now automatically mark Radar sources when they have been detected.

4. Countermeasures have now all been merged into a universal "Jamming" system. Everything works the same but now I can add "always on" jammers such as the AN/ALQ-144 which will make helicopters like the Kiowa much more resilient against IR missiles.

5. Flares and chaff now have a much better cumulative effect.

6. The Sidearm's sensor cone has now been increased as well as its turning speed. This has improved the missile's chances of detecting and hitting a Radar source quite a bit. Maximum range against a Tor is about 15km while a Shilka can be hit up to 12km away - depending on launch altitude and speed. 

The trick is still timing your launch so that the missile will get pinged by the Radar of the target you want to hit 1st. It takes a bit of practice as well as bearing in mind that the seeker on the missile activates 0.2 seconds after launch.

7. The Viper's cannon is now correctly slaved to the targeting pod again.

This pretty much wraps up the DetectionSystem beta in terms of adding new features. Please feedback comments, observations and suggestions on whether you think the Radar system is too sensitive (or not sensitive enough etc)

Assuming no major game breaking bugs, I will be pushing this build out to the main branch next week.

The next beta will be the DesertExpansion beta which will include increasing the terrain area, terrain details such as towns, bases, FARPS & airbases etc, and also building in some new mission templates to make use of the new assets.

I think after that the next beta will be looking at BLUFOR ground forces and getting them into the action which will also start the run up to the dynamic campaign!

notes.title: DetectionSystem Beta Update
notes.content:
This update integrates the VTR (Visual, Thermal, Radar) system into all units and their various detection systems.

As I mentioned before none of the current aircraft have any Radar stealth characteristics so don't expect any noticeable change in Radar detection. However, where helicopters do excel is in their thermal reduction.

For example, the Kiowa has the best thermal profile of all the helicopters and this can be seen when approaching Strelas as they will not be able to lock on at maximum range. The Kiowa can actually work 300-400m inside the Strela's engagement range safely as long as it maintains its nose towards the Strela. If it turns away then the engine exhaust will become more visible and it could find itself in a whole load of trouble!

The rest of the helicopters have profiles as you would expect with the Viper and Delta Apache having the best Thermal reductions. The Viper also has better Visual reductions to the front/rear due to its narrow profile.

The Lynx is probably the "average" helicopter and doesn't really have any particular benefit

While the Gazelle only really benefits from being the smallest helicopter and therefore the least visible. It's thermal profiles are pretty poor though due to that mainly exposed engine!

The final task I have is to integrate the VTR system into the current missiles guidance system which will then, potentially, allow you to defeat incoming IR missiles by turning to face them (although you'd have to be pretty quick though as they cover the relatively short distances very quickly). 

The main benefit of doing this, however, will be the ability simulate a whole range of Visual, Thermal & Radar jamming systems such as the AN/ALQ-144 or other ECM systems. 

And yes! I did just say "Visual" jamming systems! Think weather - such as fog, mist or other poor visibility environments that would globally effect Visual and/or Thermal targeting systems. ːsteamhappyː

Hopefully I should get the final piece of the VTR puzzle done tomorrow and, assuming no major bugs, I'll be able to send this out to the main branch.

The next Beta will be the MapExpansion beta which will be looking at expanding the current desert environment in not only physical size but also details such as airbases, civilian structures etc which should make it much more interesting to fly over.

I will also be looking at changing the terrain to real world terrain from Libya which I think will work better than the computer generated terrain the desert area currently uses.

notes.title: Update for DetectionSystem Beta
notes.content:
Finally got everything into a stable build good enough to release into the beta. This update makes a lot of very fundamental changes to the radar and detection systems in the game. These effect everything from the AH-64D's radar to the guidance systems of Hellfires so you may experience bugs!

1. Rebuilt the Radar detection system entirely so that it is now a unified detection system that can handle any type of detector whether it is Radar, Laser, Heat etc etc.

2. Decoupled the detection system from the main turret system so that turrets no longer have their own inbuilt detection system. Instead turrets are now slaved to a separate detection object.

3. Added in the AGM-144 Sidearm. This is an Anti-Radiation missile (basically a modified Sidewinder) which will home in on the 1st Radar source that it detects - you [u]cannot[/u] lock it on to a specific target. 

This makes it somewhat tricky to use and is best fired against Tor units. However, with practice you can time the launch to coincide with a particular radar ping.

4. Updated the Threat Display to help de-clutter the interface. I've reduced the saturation of the threat discs and also added a vector circle around each threat. 

5. Radar pings are now displayed for 3 seconds and fade out gradually.

6. You can now distinguish between Pulse, Doppler and PulseDoppler radars on the Threat Display.
[list]
[*] Pulse radars have a white expanding circle that animates whenever your threat display detects a an incoming source as well as the yellow line. Currently the Tor uses a Pulse Radar.
[*] Doppler radars only have the yellow line. Currently the Shilka uses a Doppler Radar
[*] PulseDoppler will have a white circle made up of dots rather than a solid line plus the yellow line. Nothing uses this radar type just yet.
[/list]

7. Incoming radar sources now use a slightly less accurate method of determining Line of Sight. This means radar shouldn't see you as easily when just peeking over the top of a hill or as you pass behind tree cover. I will be able to expose this value in the Game Settings menu to allow you to configure your own Radar LoS sensitivity shortly.

notes.title: DetectionSystem Beta Update
notes.content:
This update adds the following...

1. Threat Display background is now Black again.

2. Remade all the Radar icons to a new 32x32 pixel standard size

3. Targets with Line of Sight are now a solid colour. Targets with No LOS now have a black centre.

4. "Vectorised" the waypoint route line so it is now draw as a single pixel line no matter the zoom level of the map/threat display. It is also now white.

5. Corrected the layer tags for the trees on the Norway map so they now obey the reflection layers on the ocean.

6. By default the mouse is now locked to the game window. You can turn this off in the Game Settings menu.

notes.title: DetectionSystem Beta "Tor" Update
notes.content:
The 9K330 Tor Radar SAM system is now live in the DetectionSystem Beta and it can radically change you approach missions.

While it looks like a fairly terrifying beast of a SAM system with a Mach 2.5 missile armed with a 15kg warhead (the Strela is just 2.6kg in comparison) that can reach out to 12km, it does have its flaws.

1. It is SACLOS Radar guided which means the launching vehicle must maintain a lock on the target to guide the missile in. If a missile is launched then popping chaff, finding cover, getting very very low or destroying the launching vehicle should break the lock and the missile will miss (the missile will fly on its last programmed course so don't stay too still!).

2. It takes a surprising amount of time for the missile to cover 12km. It's average speed over the entire journey is around 500m/s (top speed is 850m/s or there about) which means you could have up to 24 seconds before the missile hits you.

3. It does have a minimum engagement range. I haven't fully tested this out but as the missile is vertically launched it does take time for it to change course. If you're close to the launcher then it may go too high and will shoot over the top of you - maybe! This is of course dependant on your relative height - the higher you are the shorter the minimum engagement range is!

4. The Radar scan rate is 10 seconds so if you time a bob-up attack correctly you can destroy the launching vehicle before it can get a missile away.

5. Tor missile system are always marked on your map. It is assumed that this systems can be detected quite easily due to their long range radar and that this information would be provided to you at the start of a mission.

6. Your Threat Display will pickup Tor Radar pings from 24km away so you'll know if they have Line of Sight to you well before you enter their engagement range.

The mission generator has been rebalanced to take into account the Tor's range and will generate missions accordingly. However, it is possible to get quite a few Tor systems on the map (or none) and/or Tor systems close to the front line which may mean you start inside their missile range! However, they shouldn't be able to target you when you're that low to the ground.

Feedback on difficulty always appreciated. This game is designed to be difficult though. Also bear in mind that there will be some dedicated weaponry coming shortly for taking out Radar systems like the Tor.

[u]Other Updates[/u]

1. Shilka's Radar can now be detected up to 5km away (twice their engagement range)

2. Missiles now have new icons on the Threat Display. Solid spinning squares are Radar guided while squares with no centres are IR guided. Small spinning squares are allied missiles.

3. The automatic countermeasure system will now deploy Chaff - however, it is much much better to manually pop chaff to get rid of Tor locks quickly.

4. Reaper drones now appear on the Threat Display correctly.

5. Trim now works correctly for helicopters

6. Radar ping lines no longer get truncated if you fly too high

notes.title: DetectionSystem Beta Update
notes.content:
This update finally makes Chaff useful and can be used to jam the Shilka's tracking radar.

I've actually now also completed the whole jamming system so it is possible to simulate not just countermeasures like chaff and flares but also things like the "Disco Light" AN/ALQ-144 IR Jammer that is present on a lot of helicopters.

1. Chaff can now jam the Shilka's tracking Radar. It is reasonably effective but it may take several dispenses to fully jam the Shilka. Chaff's jamming ability is very short lived so it is quite possible for a jammed shilka to re-acquire you again pretty quickly.

2. Chaff now makes a noise when dispensed.

3. The Kiowa now has its "Hero" external model.

4. The Kiowa now has water interaction settings.

5. Tweaked the Kiowa's drag and lift settings so it can now obtain a reasonable forward speed when fully loaded.

notes.title: DetectionSystem Beta Hotfix
notes.content: Reverts the Threat Display background colour back to grey. Seems I didn't think the colour change through quite enough!! ːsteamfacepalmː

notes.title: DetectionSystem beta update
notes.content:
This update is another important milestone as it adds in the Threat Display's ability to detect enemy Radar transmissions (which is also a key feature required by Stealth Fighter D.E.X)

These transmissions will be displayed as a white line between your helicopter and the source on the Threat Display. You will also hear an audio "blip" each time the Threat Display detects a Radar transmission even if the Threat Display is not currently displayed on the MFDs.

Single "blips" indicate a search radar has hit you and the line will be visible on the Threat Display for about 1 second before fading. 

When your helicopter gets locked by Radar you will hear a continuous warning sound plus a constant line displayed on the Threat Display showing you where the threat is coming from.

Your Threat Display can detect Radar transmission far outside the red threat circle (about 6km for Shilkas) so you now get fair warning where these vehicles are hiding. Of course, detecting them requires line of sight so it is still possible for a Shilka to ambush you but at least now you'll know where the threat is coming from!

Unfortunately Chaff still doesn't effect anything - I just ran out of time to get that working this week. Next week I will definitely be getting that and the Tor missile system working and in game.

[u]Other Updates[/u]

1. Fixed some script errors for the rockets.

2. Fixed the bloom effect for tracers which some how got messed up in the last update.

3. Increased the Rotor Drag values for the Apache

4. Updated the "Fly By" cam so that it can handle fast moving objects e.g. Harrier. It will also no longer appear under the ground when your sitting on the helipad allowing you to view takeoffs.

5. The initial selected helicopter is now always the AH-64D Apache.

notes.title: DetectionSystem beta update
notes.content:
This update adds the following...

1. Chaff! You can now launch chaff from your aircraft! Currently it doesn't actually do anything but the particle effects are there.

2. You can now turn off the underwater effects in the Video Settings menu. Turning Underwater Effects OFF will give a noticeable FPS boost but makes the water completely opaque so that you cannot see anything below the surface from above. It also removes the underwater effects when the camera goes below the water's surface.

3. Fixed a few HUD font size issues

4. Parking Brakes are now released automatically when retracting the Harrier's landing gear.

5. All destroyable objects now have a 360 degree Visual, Thermal and Radar (VTR) signature. This currently doesn't effect anything but will do in the next update :) 

6. All particle effects have bee optimised to be more performant. I've also implemented some constraints that will limit screen over draw / fill rate issues encountered when particles cover a large portion of the screen e.g. when flying through smoke

7. Fixed some layering issues with explosion dust rings. They should no longer appear drawn over other particle effects even when far away.

8. Optimised various 3D models that still had left over / un-used meshes.

9. Threat Display background colour is now black rather than grey

10. Altered some of the rendering systems so that Norway doesn't look quite so washed out.

11. Removed ocean reflections from being visible in the targeting pod camera view.

12. Update the Rotor Disc physics system to include drag calculations. This prevents helicopters from simply falling out of the sky when at 0% power. They will now come down in a slightly more controller manner! This also allows helicopters to decelerate much faster. 

13. Updated Rotor Disc physics with Angle of Attack lift calculations. This allows the main rotors to generate extra lift from forward motion if you pitch up enough. This allows you to "flare" landings and even perform a "semi-autorotational" landing if you have enough forward momentum.

notes.title: Update for DetectionSystem beta
notes.content:
This update adds the following...

1. Updated the camera movement system so that it will move smoothly even when the aircraft if flying quickly. This mainly effected the Harrier and caused little stutters when rotating the outside views.

2. Updated the HUD to make it more readable

3. Added "Units of Measurement" to the Game Options menu allowing to choose your preferred Speed (kts, mph, km/h), Height (m or ft) and Distance (m or yds) measurements. The current Speed and Altitude units are now displayed next to the related readout on the HUD.

4. Fixed a slight bug in the ID system which would sometimes cause a destroyed vehicle to stay on the threat display. 

5. Added a new music track

6. Added ASL (Above Sea Level) altitude readout to the top of the Altimeter ticker tape. The Radar altimeter is now limited to 999 m or ft 

This will be last update for a few days while I'm away from my development machine.

notes.title: Update for DetectionSystem Beta
notes.content:
This update adds the following...

1. Fixed the ID system so that 100% identified vehicles will now be correctly marked on the threat display.

2. You must have direct line of sight to ID targets so you can no longer ID them through the terrain when targeting them via the Threat Display.

3. When vehicles open fire there is now a chance they will be instantly detected by your C/PG. Different vehicles have different detection chances with the Shilka and Strela both having high detection chances. This is to simulate your gunner being able to follow the smoke/tracer trail back to its source. IFVs, APCs & tanks have a much lower detection chance.

4. Fixed a bug in the turret control system which was causing all A.I. vehicles to shoot high. Downside is everything is more accurate with Shilkas being particularly nasty at high A.I. skill levels.

5. Added an axis control for the Trim function so those with a proper trim wheel (or any non-centering controller axis) can now use it to control the trim function. Please note that if you do assign an axis then this will override all other Trim controls.

notes.title: Update for DetectionSystem Beta
notes.content:
The update adds the following....

1. Added in Trim Up, Down & Reset controls.

2. Trim level is now displayed on the HUD below the wheel brakes. Not sure if it is going to stay there, but at least you can see your trim levels.

3. Upgraded the Hydra 70 & APKWS 3D models to the new Hi-Def models - no more blue cubes! Next thing is to add in some camera views so you can actually admire the new models!

4. Optimised the trees on the Norway map which should reduce memory usage by a significant amount. It should also speed up loading times for that map too.

notes.title: DetectionSystem beta update
notes.content:
This update adds the following....

1. New Pitch Trim option. This allows you to do a basic pitch trim on all aircraft where you find yourself having to constantly hold a pitch input to keep it level. The Harrier is the worse offender for this.

To set the trim simply hold the aircraft level then press the "Pitch Trim" button "Trim" MFD option. This will save the current vertical input and apply it as a constant offset. Release your controls and you should find the aircraft is now trimmed and doesn't require constant input - or at least much less. The set trim is generally only valid for the current airspeed so as you speed up or slow down you may need to re-trim.

To clear the trim simply press the trim button with no input applied.

2. Free Flight mode. There is now a new mission called "Free Flight". It will setup a basic mission for you but none of the enemy units will fire back. You can use this mission template to practice flying and using the weapons, sensors and support units.

The mission is fully functional in that you can complete both the primary and secondary targets - however, no score will be added to your pilots.

[u]Upcoming Update[/u]

Next week I will be doing some updates to some of the missiles/rockets 3d models. I will also be finishing off the Tor missile system although this may not make it into the update as I will be away from my development machine from Wednesday for a few days so will have limited ability to fix anything that might go wrong with it!

notes.title: DetectionSystem Beta Update
notes.content:
A few updates and fixes for the DetectionSystem Beta....

1. Corrected the MTOW calculation for the Harrier. The MTOW relates to the maximum vertical takeoff weight. It is possible to exceed the weight if you can find a flat area to do a rolling takeoff.

2. Added vapour trail effects to the Harrier when performing turns.

3. Harrier now loses speed in tight turns rather than gaining it!

4. Rockets now have a flatter trajectory

5. Changed the shadows for the rotor blades so they are not the horrible pixel dot effect which is Unity's attempt at rendering shadows for semi-transparent objects. Not 100% if I like it any better though!

***hotifx***

1. Minor tweak to the high speed wing root vapour trails

notes.title: Harrier Update for DetectionSystem Beta
notes.content:
Yes! It's real!

This update adds a Harrier GR.9 to the flyable aircraft list. It is not just a helicopter re-skin - it really does fly like an aircraft.

That being said - please be aware that this is really only a tech demo of getting the current flight model to transition from a helicopter to a normal aircraft and, as such, the flight model is a little twitchy!

The nozzle vectoring is currently all controlled automatically for you so you'll need to take this into account as you attempt to transition into forward flight. This is the basic procedure....

1. Rise vertically to about 50m altitude
2. Raise landing gear
3. Dip nose to begin forward acceleration
4. Once you've achieved 70-80kts of forward speed the thrust vectoring should now provide enough forward power to be able to climb and accelerate away.
5. At around 180kts the transition from hover to forward flight is complete and you are now flying as a normal aircraft (or there abouts!)

Because there is no trim system the Harrier will feel nose heavy at low speed but will want to climb at high speed - this is something I will work on in the future.

Other considerations is that none of the weapons are really designed for fast movers. Hellfires can sometimes struggle to hit correctly if launched at close range or very high speed. However, the twin ADEN canon is a lot of fun!

For those that are wondering why I've put the Harrier in a helicopter game - I needed to develop a suitable hybrid flight mode for both the Cheyenne and Osprey helicopters/VTOLs. Doing a Harrier seemed logical and I also had a 3d model available!

The build also allowed me to create animation systems for hydraulic systems such as the control surfaces and landing gear which are also required for some upcoming helicopters.

Plus - it also allowed me to see how the missions system/terrain areas worked with fixed wing aircraft as a guide to how much work is required to setup Stealth Fighter D.E.X.

[u]Other Updates[/u]

1. Added a new music track

2. Unified the map icon system so that they scale correctly when zooming maps in and out

3. Missiles now appear on the threat display system (work in progress - I need to make them more visible)

[u]Other News[/u]

The Tor SAM system didn't quite make it. The vehicle is in and the missiles are working together with a suitable command guidance system, but I didn't have time to setup the chaff system which would mean you'd have no defence against them.

I will get that sorted ASAP - maybe over the weekend if I have time but, if not, certainly early next week.

[u]Hotfix[/u]

1. Corrected the Harrier's targeting pod gimbal limits to help prevent it targeting itself!

2. Removed the HUD meshes from the Harrier cockpit as they are not needed and were causing issues with the ocean renderer due to back face culling.

[u]Hotfix 2[/u]

1. Fixed an issue with the Stores page not refreshing correctly when starting a new mission.

1. You should no longer see "gaps" in the ocean around the TOW missile launchers.

2. Ocean should no longer flicker and/or disappear in some areas.

This update effects both the public branch and the new DetectionSystem beta.

[*] OH-58D Kiowa Warrior to the flyable helicopter list. It is a light scout helicopter where its main strength lies in its mast mounted site which will allow you to remain totally undetected when scouting out areas.

There's not a huge amount I can do about it at the moment as solving the issue would require me to build some memory management systems which would take a fair bit of time to develop. 

However, it is something that I [u]definitely do[/u] need to fix as it will become more of an issue when dealing with very large terrain areas (e.g. those needed by Stealth Figher D.E.X) so I will be sorting it out before too long.

notes.title: Norway Beta Update
notes.content:
Quite a few things in this update...

1. Fixed the Hellfires attack profile so that it will correctly account for its current launch altitude.

2. Updated the loadout for the Kiowa so that it only has 2 hard points.

3. Fixed the HUD waypoint icon, targeting pod icon and artificial horizon so that they are not displayed when their position is behind the current camera view. This should prevent confusion on where the targeting pod is looking when flying the Kiowa.

4. Implemented texture streaming to help reduce VRAM usage as it was getting a bit high with all those 4k textures!

5. Added some new options to the Video Settings menu so that you can control the amount of VRAM used by textures plus change the overall texture quality. For most people you can leave it at its default settings but if you have a GPU with less than 4Gb VRAM then this can help you limit the amount used by textures which should prevent any out of VRAM crashes.

Here's a more detailed explanation of each setting...

[list]
[*] Texture Quality - this sets the maximum resolution used for all textures. Generally you should just leave it on FULL and the texture streaming system will then work out what to load until it hits the VRAM usage limit. When this happens it will load lower detailed textures automatically to keep within the VRAM usage limit.

[*] Max VRAM Usage - this limits the total amount of VRAM the texture streaming system will use. The higher this is set the more high quality textures will be loaded into VRAM. I would recommend setting this to 50% of your total GPU VRAM to start. 

For computers which shared VRAM (e.g. Steam Deck) set it to 2048Mb and see how you get on. If you encounter crashes then decrease it. If you encounter blurry textures then increase it.
[/list]

6. Water settings should now be saved and loaded correctly.

This update adds the OH-58D Kiowa Warrior to the flyable helicopter list.

It is a light scout helicopter where its main strength lies in its mast mounted site which will allow you to remain totally undetected when scouting out areas.

The Kiowa is not a particularly fast helicopter (roughly 130kts flat out unloaded) and it does not have a very big load capacity (around 1,000kg depending on fuel levels) which can make it a bit of a tricky helicopter to master.

At the moment it costs 35 DP which may need rebalancing. I have also rebalanced the Gazelle's DP points  slightly.

notes.title: Norway Terrain Beta Bug Fixes
notes.content:
This update addresses a number of bugs in the Norway terrain beta...

1. Pilot scores are now added correctly at the end of the mission as long as you compete either your primary or secondary missions.

2. Water reflections are now culled correctly in the targeting pod view

3. "Vectorised" the targeting pod icon and radar cursor on the threat display MFD screen so they no longer flicker occassionally.

4. Corrected the position of the targeting pod icon on the threat display so it now matches correctly when changing the threat display range.

5. Updated the intercept guidance script of the Strela so that it is much less likely to fly into the ground when trying to calculate an intercept point. This has been done by limiting its angle of interception to within its seekers gimbal limits. This is much more realistic and, if you're flying fast enough perpendicular to it, you may now be able to evade the missile - maybe!

Other known bugs....

1. The targeting pod has a habit of jittering. Not sure what it causing this but it is more noticeable at low frame rates.

2. Hellfires do not take into account their launch altitude which makes using them from high positions (e.g. on to of a Norwegian mountain) problematic as they will not do a top down attack properly and instead fly fairly flat.

notes.title: Norway Beta Update
notes.content:
This update does the following....

1. Retextures the Norway terrain using something approaching "Satellite" imagery rather than the more abstract textures I was using before. The result is something far closer to what the island actually looks like in real life. 

For those who want to cross reference the island it is here...

https://www.google.com/maps/@70.6180847,22.5991863,52400m/data=!3m1!1e3

2. Added a new ground texture under where trees appear

3. Improved the snow textures

4. Tweaked a few of the terrain splat mapping parameters so that things like rocks now peak out from beneath snow/grass on steep slopes and grass itself grows a little higher up the mountains on the flatter parts.

5. Desaturated the trees a little to make them blend a little better.

6. Fixed FPS drop when zooming the camera in - this is actually a major fix as I was limited on how much of a zoom a camera could have because the more the camera zoomed the lower your FPS would go. This now fixes the Unity terrain error that causes this and any FPS drop should now be minimal.

This also allows me to set different camera zoom levels for different helicopters with the possibility of more advanced helicopters having better camera zoom levels.

notes.title: Norway Beta Update
notes.content:
This update enables mission generation on the new Norway terrain as well as....

1. Fixed a bug where trees wouldn't show up in the targeting pod view

2. Fixed a bug where the stores page would not show any weapons

3. Updated enemy A.I. so that trees will occlude their vision. This is also true for your radar and CP/G spotting ability.

3. All MFD maps will now be hidden correctly

Missions work exactly as they do on the Lush Desert terrain. However, due to the mountainous nature of Norway, mission can be a lot longer unless you want to fly over the top of the mountains which can be a little risky!

notes.title: Norway Terrain Beta Update
notes.content:
This update adds the following....

1. All trees to all terrain tiles

2. Fixed the topographical map generation for Norway so that it now takes into account sea levels.

3. Updated the radar altitude system to take into account sea level. This is just the average sea level and does not take into account wave heights!

4. Added the following to the Video Settings menu...

[list]
[*] Terrain Resolution - allows you to reduce the resolution of the height map used for terrain generation. This reduces the number of polygons that makes up the terrain.
[*] Pixel Error - this adjust the level of terrain resolution for distant terrain. Higher numbers result in higher frame rates but lower accuracy of distant terrain which can cause visual "popping".
[*] Terrain Shadows - enables or disables terrain self shadowing

[*] Water Quality - allows you choose the resolution of the water mesh.
[*] Water Reflections - allows you to choose what is reflected in the water reflections. Reflections are hugely resource intensive so default is OFF. However, you can set it to Sky Only which is still fairly performant but will give greater accuracy to water colouring from sun/moon light.
[*] Reflection Resolution- allows you to choose the quality of the water reflection.

[*] View Distance - allows you to choose how far into the distance things are drawn. This mainly effects terrain and atmosphere/clouds. 

The game is optimised for 20km but I think most people will be able to crank this up higher. It does not effect the "Player Bubble" size which is set to 15km so you won't gain any advantage/disadvantage to spotting enemy vehicles etc.
[/list]

Tomorrow I will be placing the mission markers over the main island which will allow all current mission templates to generate missions on the new terrain.

Feedback on performance is always welcome ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Norway Terrain Beta Update
notes.content:
A couple of fixes and updates....

1. Fixed the slightly amusing bug where turning off the Map on the Threat Display also removed the in game terrain from view!

2. Ocean colour now respects the correct sun/moon light so it no longer looks like it is glowing at night.

3. Adjusted the foam effects slightly.

4. Improved the origin shifting system so that it can handle the huge number of tree colliders without creating a small "hiccup" pause in the game. This is actually a really important development as shifting this many objects in a single go has always been problematic in Unity but I think I now have a working solution for it. ːsteamhappyː

Next week I will be finalising the tree generation system by adding in some tree variations. I will also be looking at whether the system can be expanded to include other terrain details such as bushes and rocks etc without reducing FPS too much or, at the very least, being a toggleable visual option.

I shall also start adding in the mission markers so the mission generators will know where to place things. Hopefully this won't take as long as the Lush Desert as there will simply be less suitable flat areas available due to the terrain topology.

Once this is done I think it will be time for a physics simulation pass as there are a number of things I'm not happy with in terms of the helicopter's flight models.

I'm very pleased with the progress that I'm making on the game and, hopefully, so are you ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Norway Terrain Beta
notes.content:
The Front Lines beta has now been replaced with the Norway Terrain Beta.

You will need to re-opt in as I can't change Beta names unfortunately. Usual opt in steps are as follows...

1. Right Click on the game and select "Properties"
2. On the new window select "Betas"
3. Then select "norwayterrain Norway Terrain Beta" from the drop down.
4. Do not enter a password, just close the window and you should get the update.

When you run the game you should now find you have "Norway" in the Location drop down menu.

This will then enter you into a free flight mode for the new Norway terrain. Enjoy the new scenery and there might be something interesting to the South / South East of your starting location....

I have also added in the new tree models that I made which are extremely fast to render. They're obviously not super detailed but the fact I can have 25,000 on screen at the same time with a minimal performance hit makes them worth while and finally I can do quite dense forests - they also look better than the green pyramids in yesterday's pictures!

I do need to address the fact that they are all the same model but that's all the time I had today!

All trees have colliders but they are generally forgiving in their collision detection. Essentially it is only the main trunk that you will actually hit - the outer branches are assumed to be fairly inconsequential! Hopefully there are no invisible trees (EECH2 fans!!)

[u]Performance[/u]

Early testing seems to indicate that the game now runs a little faster than it did before! Even with all the trees, ocean simulation and the terrain running at 4x the resolution of the Lush Desert zone I get 250fps+ reported by Steam at 1080p (RTX 2080ti / i9 9900K).

The Lush Desert area also received a bit of a performance boost as I fixed a few things which had a global impact on performance ːsteamhappyː

Please feedback on your own experience...

[u]Known Bugs[/u]

1. Map is not currently drawn on either the mission briefing or MFD screens.

2. At night the water looks like it is glowing!

3. You can fly underwater!

4. Trees are identical currently apart from sizing. I will be addressing this later on so that there is some variation!

notes.title: Various Updates for Front Lines Beta

notes.title: Update for Front Lines Beta
notes.content:
Mostly a tidy up and bug fix update today...

1. Fixed the T-62M's turret rotation axis so that it now rotates correctly

2. Added a "Ballistic" status to missiles so that when they miss their target they won't attempt to do a 180 degree turn and come back. This effects all guided missiles from TOWs to Strelas.

3. Fixed the gravity calculation for missiles so that as they slow down they will start to lose altitude.

4. Fixed the spelling of "Fuselage"

5. Unified all vehicle Hit Points so that soft targets have 20Hp, Lightly Armoured have 40Hp and Heavy Armour has 100Hp. The differences between units of the same type will then be down to their specific armour values.

6. TOW, HOT and Hellfire missiles now have a small blast radius which might take out soft targets that are close to the impact point.

7. TOW & HOT missiles have had their "snaking" flight path tweaked to be more realistic.

8. 30mm HEDP rounds now have a small blast radius making them much more effective against soft targets as a near miss will still do some damage.

9. Weight of the Hydra and APKWS have now been corrected to the real world values.

10. Added 19 x APKWS rocket pod for the Apache D. While it sounds great to have 19 guided munitions it is balanced by being heavy (heavier than 4 Hellfire "R" missiles) and significantly more expensive!

[u]IMPORTANT[/u]

Later this week I will be deploying the 1st set of pilot images. Anyone who is already using custom pilot images should make a copy of them because when I deploy the new ones, the old ones will be overwritten.

It is always worth making a backup of custom pilot images because even running a file validation in Steam will overwrite them.

notes.title: Update for Frontlines Beta
notes.content:
1. Modified the way the Smart Boresight system works so that it has two modes "Scanning" and "Locked" which are shown on the targeting camera's display.

When in "Scanning" mode it will be looking for targets near the area under the centre of the HUD. Once it finds a target it will automatically lock on to the target allowing you to engage it. It will no longer switch to another target automatically. Instead, when you are ready for a new target, you can press the "Lock Target" button to put the Smart Boresight back into "Scanning" mode where it will search for targets again.

This places you directly in control of what is being targeted and prevents the system from jumping to a new target unintentionally such as during a missile launch!

It is worth noting that the Smart Boresight if using the centre of the HUD - not the nose of the helicopter or where the targeting pod is pointed. This allows you to use it with TrackIR (as an IHADSS replacement if you don't like the overlay) or the move camera controls so you can lock things up with Smart Boresight by rotating the view camera around!

I will be adding secondary mode that works using the targeting camera view point.

2. Fixed a bug where the targeting camera would sometimes end up pointing to the upper right of its gimbal limits. This was the targeting pod trying to lock up itself! It shouldn't happen any more.

3. Modified the flight model for the SA-349 as it felt very under powered and didn't seem to want to climb very well.

Unfortunately I didn't have time to build any mission to take advantage of the new spotting mechanic as I've been really busy managing other things such as missile models and portrait artists and I've no idea where this week went!!

So this weeks update feels a little on the light side but I will try to make it up next week ːsteamhappyː

BTW I should have good news on another flyable helicopter and the only clue I'm giving you is "Wyoming"!!

notes.title: Target IDing Update for Front Lines Beta
notes.content:
This update adds the Target IDing system allowing you to manually ID targets by targeting them yourself.

When a target is locked using the targeting pod camera your gunner will attempt to identify it for you. This can take some time depending on your gunner skill and distance to target. Anything over 8km is going to take a while for low level gunners. 

Your targeting pod view will show how close to identifying the target your gunner is by displaying a value from 0% - 100%

Once identified, the targeting pod will show that actual target type e.g. BMP-1 plus the target will be marked on your threat display allowing you to build a picture of the enemy units around you and target them quickly using the threat display.

Targets that get automatically marked on your threat display e.g. by Radar or your CP/G will instantly be 100% identified.

While this update only seems small it does pave the way for recon missions where you need to identify targets rather than destroying them. I hope to get some of these mission types built tomorrow. ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: APKWS Update for Front Lines Beta
notes.content:
This update adds the APKWS (Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System) to the game.

This basically adds a laser guidance to a 70mm rocket making it just as accurate as something like a Hellfire at the expense of weight and cost (approx. 10kg & 15 Dp per rocket).

They come in pods of 7 rockets and are available to all Advanced Tech helicopters (AH-64D, AH-1Z, Lynx 3 & SA-349 Gazelle).

Usage is just like a laser guided Hellfire except they travel much faster and therefore have a narrower launch window. They are quite manoeuvrable though.

Range is set to 5,000m but they should be able to travel much further.

They are designed to be used against soft and lightly armoured targets in their current High Explosive format (I shall also be adding Armour Piercing varieties shortly) with a single rocket usually being enough to take out a BMP-1. T-62Ms will require several rockets meaning TOW, HOT & Hellfire missiles are still a better option against heavy armour.

[u][b]Armour Values[/b][/u]

This also brings me to the other main feature of this update - Armour Values!

All vehicles now have an armour value and all weapons have an armour penetration value. This is used to calculate the damage dealt by the weapon against an armoured target.

The formula is quite simple and is as follows...

WeaponDamage / (1 + (ArmourValue - ArmourPenetration))

[u]For Example[/u]
A 30mm HEDP round fired by the Apache has an armour penetration value of 2 and a damage value of 5 to 10.

A BMP-1 has an armour value of 2 and 40 hit points

So a single hit on a BMP-1 will be 10 / (1 + (2 - 2)) = 10 / 1 = 10

In this particular case the 30mm round has enough armour penetration to defeat the BMP-1s armour so it does full damage and will therefore take 4 hits to kill assuming it always does max damage.

What this means in practice is that heavily armoured units will be more resistant to smaller weapons but it also introduces a nice mechanic where shortly you will need to think about the types of warheads equipped to weapons.

Should you take HE rockets for area effect or AP rockets for punching through armour?

Your helicopter also benefits from these calculations so the Apache should feel a little less squishy against 23mm rounds and all helicopters in general should be a little more survivable.

notes.title: Front Lines Beta Update
notes.content:
This update adds a new targeting mechanic to the game - the "Smart Boresight".

You can enable this targeting mode via the targeting pods MFD using Modifier 1 plus MFD Button 6. You can also setup a key binding for it in the Control Settings menu called "Toggle Smart Boresight".

When in this mode the targeting pod will display the targeting square, the LASER notification as well as a new SMART BORE notification just below.

The system works by checking for any objects along a 3km path from the centre of the current camera view. If an object is detected (e.g. terrain) then the targeting system will scan for any targets within a 100m radius of that point. The target closest to that point is then automatically locked up.

In practice this means you just point the camera near a target and the targeting pod will snap to it. The system is smart enough to know if a target is dead or not and will switch to the next available target if one is available making strafing runs much easier as there is no need to slew the targeting pod manually.

This system is basically simulating having a Co-pilot making sensible decisions on what target your are probably after and will form the basis of the Auto-Targeting mode which will allow you to hand off turret control to your gunner's A.I. completely.

The Smart Boresight also works in a similar way to IHADSS but without the overlay and I will upgrade the IHADSS system to use this same "snapping" system to allow more easy targeting but with a narrower scanning radius.

[u]Other Updates[/u]

1. Overhaul of the targeting cameras logic to make the Smart Bore system work. This also allowed me to make some tweaks which hopefully should prevent the weird issue of the targeting pod getting locked into the top corner of its gimbal limits sometimes.

2. All locked targets are now automatically re-acquired after going outside the gimbal limits whereas before only Radar locked targets would do this.

3. Selected Pilot/Co-pilots in the Mission Planning phase are now remembered even after restarting the game.

4. If you select a Default pilot or co-pilot then you will get a warning message before starting the mission advising you to choose a custom pilot (you don't have to though).

[u]Meaningful Update[/u]

This week's meaningful update was supposed to include the Su-25 and stingers. Unfortunately I don't think I'm going to complete those in time so instead, and to compliment the Smart Boresight, I'll be adding in the APKWS (and probably the DAGR) weapon systems which should open up even more options on how you tackle missions.

If I have time I will also be adding the vertical aim system to the existing Hydra 70 pods.

notes.title: Front Lines Beta Beautification Update!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42621381/1f65163367c9f743c04f29db7fcafcb0ffb21d83.jpg[/img]

In addition I have also modified the way the TOW is launched to more closely replicate the real world version. 

Essentially it is a 2 stage launch with an initial charge propelling the missile out of the launcher then, approximately 0.5 seconds later, the main rocket motor ignites accelerating the missile towards its target.

All TOW launchers are now inclined at 5 degrees to assist the initial launch and it is more important than ever to use the launch reticule to ensure your target is within flight parameters. 

Minimum launch altitude is about 15m anything less and the missile may not recover lost altitude but it is also dependant on range to target and the target's relative height to your helicopter.

[u]Other Updates[/u]

1. I've tweaked the Combat Lynx's loadout as the Hydra 70 rocket pod was too big for the inner pylons and could cause it to bounce around on the helipad. Instead the inner pylons get SNEBs and the outer pylons SNEBs or HYDRAs

notes.title: AH-1Z Viper for the Front Lines Beta
notes.content:

notes.title: Front Lines BETA Update
notes.content:
This update adds and fixes the following...

1. Toggling IHADSS will now display an overlay from the targeting pod on the HUD. It lines up pretty well with the real world as long as your head position in the cockpit is centred and the pod is on its "Wide" zoom level.

There is still some offset due to the pods location on each helicopter so objects very close will be more obviously misaligned. This is also true when in 3rd person mode.

2. IHADSS will no longer automatically disable itself when you've exceeded the pods gimbal limits. The pod will re-establish tracking once you're back inside the gimbal limits.

3. Locking a target while using IHADSS will not disable the IHADSS overlay allowing you to fine tune aiming using the pods slew controls.

4. New option in the Game Settings menu to toggle the "Resize MFD" control between physically zooming into the In-Cockpit MFDs or adjusting the virtual MFD sizes as normal. 

This option, together with the "Auto Hide Virtual MFDs" option, gives you 3 different modes for the MFDs when in cockpit view....

1. Virtual MFDs are shown in the in-cockpit view and continue to work as normal. Using "Resize MFD" simply scales their size on screen.

2. Virtual MFDs are shown in the in-cockpit view but using "Resize MFD" zooms you to the physical MFD screen.

3. Virtual MFDs are disabled when in cockpit view and using "Resize MFD" zooms you to the physical MFD screen. 

This also fixes the bug where cycling the MFD when in cockpit view would instantly zoom the view to the MFD.

5. Fixed the Field of View sliders so that the camera instantly updates to the new value when clicking the Save button rather than requiring a view change.

notes.title: Front Lines Performance Update
notes.content:
This update fixes a few of the performance issues related to the much larger number of units on the field.

1. Updated LOD levels for all vehicles to bring the total mesh rendering down to sensible levels.

2. Updated the map icon image system to be much more performant. Surprisingly this is actually where I made most performance gains - seems my code for the radar icons etc was rubbish!!

3. Restored the IR signatures for vehicles so they are now clearly visible once again.

4. Added a helicopter image to the mission planning map so you can see where you are.

5. Allowed the mission planning map to show all detected vehicles etc

6. Removed the fading of contacts over time. Now, once you've detected a vehicle it will remain detected forever. However, the positional information will only update on a successful Radar or visual ping from the C/PG. 

This doesn't effect anything at the moment as all vehicles are stationary but, in the future, when they do move launching a Radar Hellfire missile at an old or NOLOS contact may result in a miss if the target vehicle has moved far enough to be outside the Hellfire's scanning arc.

7. Improved the spread of the Apache's 30mm gun so it can engage targets a bit further out.

notes.title: Introducing the AH.7 Lynx!
notes.content:
While I'm working on the Front Lines system I thought it'd be nice to give you another helicopter to play with.

The AH.7 sits nicely in between the Apache and the Gazelle as a light attack helicopter. It's fast but can carry 8 TOWs and still have room for 2 x 20mm gun pods! It can also mount HYDRA 70 Rocket pods instead of TOW missiles if you wish.

The helicopter is fully functional but currently uses the same engine sound from the Gazelle. I'll sort a proper replacement tomorrow.

The Lynx is also using a modified rotor flight model which allows it to dive and climb better when moving at speed. I think it feels much better than the current Gazelle flight model - but let me know what you think.

[u][b]Other Fixes[/b][/u]

1. Zooming into the MFDs while in the 3D cockpit now disables the dynamic camera movement so the displays don't move around due to helicopter movement.

2. Relative collective controls now work correctly when using autopilots and trying to set the target altitude.

notes.title: Minor Update
notes.content:
This update allows you to set the Cyclic X Power, Cyclic Y Power and Tail Rotor Power to less than 100% (minimum 10%) in the Game Settings menu.

This is a different way of reducing the sensitivity of controls  by actually limiting the maximum input power rather than by adjusting the Helicopter Stability which is physics based.

If your controls feel over sensitive then these options should allow you to tweak it to your preference.

notes.title: Happy New Year! Relative Collective + Other Improvements
notes.content:
1. I have now added a Relative Collective option in the Game Settings menu. Works as you'd expect and allows you to set a collective amount rather than having to hold your input at the desired level.

This is mainly for Gamepad users who, due to the centring spring on the sticks, have to continually hold the collective on to fly effectively which can become tiring. Altitude Hold does alleviate most of this already but some may prefer this level of control instead.

2. I have also added an "Enable Extended Joypad Modifiers" option in the Game Settings menu. Extended modifiers are controls which cannot be rebound and do not show up in the Control Settings menu. They are really for advanced users and can cause confusion etc which is why they must be manually enabled.

The 1st extended control is "Collective Look" which can be enabled by holding Modifier 2 and clicking Cycle View button. This will then allow your Collective/Tail Rotor control stick to control the camera view. 

This is really designed for Gamepad users who currently have no way of looking around without using the mouse, keyboard or TrackIR

Obviously this should only be done when using Altitude Hold / Hover Hold!!

3. Animated  Flight Sticks! All cockpits now have an animated flight stick which follows your cyclic input.

4. I've also written some guides...
Gamepad Control Guide
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2910713794
Walks you though how the Gamepad control system, modifiers and Screen of Interest systems work.

Helicopter Guide
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2908499881
Details all the helicopters currently available in game

notes.title: Camera View Update
notes.content:
This update makes a number of improvements to the way you can control the camera in-game...

1. You can now bind mouse axis in the Control Settings menu. By default the game will use the mouse to control the camera rotation. However, because this has been added in just now you'll need to bind the mouse axis manually or click the "Restore Defaults" button to reset all controls.

This now supersedes the old "Mouse Look" option in the Game Settings menu and so this has been removed. The speed sliders do still work though so you can to tweak those to your preferred settings.

You can also bind the mouse to the cyclic to control the helicopters but it's not really recommended. I will be developing better mouse controls shortly.

2. There are now some new camera controls in the Control Settings menu....
[list]
[*] Camera Horizontal Position - allows you to reposition the camera left & right. Also works in cockpit view.
[*] Camera Vertical Position - allows you to reposition the camera up & down. Also works in cockpit view.
[*] Ext. Camera Dolly - allows you to move the camera forwards & backwards. Only works in external chase cam.
[/list]

These allow you to position the camera to your own preference. Want an "over the shoulder" external chase cam. You can do that! Need to move the pilot's seat position higher up? You can do that too!

Positions are not saved between missions.

3. Cockpit MFD Physical Zoom

You can now zoom into the the cockpit MFDs in the same way as the virtual MFDs e.g. by using the "Cycle MFD Sizes" key or "Modifier 1 + MFD Button 1". There is only a single zoom level but it basically makes the MFD full screen.

The main HUD remains overlaid on the screen so you can keep an eye on altitude and autopilot modes etc.

4. Flares now make a sound when being launched!

notes.title: Various Updates

This is the final patch before the Christmas Break. Thank you to all those who have supported this project so far. I'll be picking up development again in about a weeks time ːsteamhappyː

2. You can now delete waypoints that you have created by right clicking on them in the Mission Planning screen

Thank you once again for you support ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Small patch

notes.title: Minor tweaks and changes
notes.content:
1. Changed the way Deadzone works on the control bindings so that it separates X & Y axis properly.

2. Changed the way Sensitivity works so that it also works on separate axis.

3. Sensitivity also works slightly differently. Instead of it limiting the overall amount of input it now changes the amount of movement required. A low sensitivity (less than 1) will give you more control over small movement changes while a high sensitivity (greater than 1) will do the opposite.

4. Waypoints should no longer sometimes become un-draggable.
